displayContract.byline: Assessments made by 5.6 Sol. — Rubric: Slugfester Reassessment Rubric v2.

thesis.text: The strongest EAAN case is that naturalism and evolution, without a separately justified truth-linking account, leave reflective believers unable to retain warranted confidence in the general reliability of the faculties underwriting that worldview.

novelty.explanation: This steelman replaces an unsupported categorical probability claim with a conditional demand for a separately justified reliability bridge.

premises.text: Natural selection directly filters heritable systems by reproductive consequences, so semantic truth receives evolutionary support only insofar as some defensible mechanism connects accurate representation with adaptively successful behavior.

novelty.explanation: This develops the transcript's selection-target distinction while allowing indirect selection for accuracy rather than denying it by stipulation.

premises.text: Conceptual and causal constraints may restrict which content can accompany a neural state, but restriction alone does not establish that the admissible content corresponds accurately to the external environment.

novelty.explanation: This integrates the strongest con constraints while preserving Plantinga's narrower determination-versus-correspondence objection.

premises.text: A reliability judgment should concern calibrated performance across cognitive domains, dependencies, and error patterns, rather than multiplying independent fifty-percent probabilities across an undifferentiated collection of beliefs.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the unsupported independence and equal-odds assumptions in the transcript's compound-probability presentation.

premises.text: If a reflective naturalist lacks adequate grounds for a sufficiently broad truth-conducive connection, that higher-order doubt can undercut reliance on faculties when evaluating the worldview that generated the doubt.

novelty.explanation: This narrows automatic defeat propagation to reflective higher-order doubt and avoids assuming that every particular belief is uniformly defeated.

premises.text: Theism can offer a purposive reliability expectation only if its broader evidential case supports a creator whose intentions include generally dependable cognition despite acknowledged human fallibility and error.

novelty.explanation: This makes the theistic contrast conditional on total evidence instead of treating divine reliability purposes as automatic.

conclusion.text: Accordingly, naturalism and evolution face an epistemic self-defeat challenge when their believer cannot independently justify a sufficiently general connection between evolved cognitive organization and truth-conducive performance.

novelty.explanation: This preserves the rational-acceptance conclusion while making it conditional on failure to justify the disputed reliability connection.

newArguments.title: The domain-transfer challenge
newArguments.text: Evolutionary success most directly rewards cognition in recurrent, fitness-relevant environments, yet the worldview-level beliefs involved in naturalism, evolutionary theory, probability, and metaphysics extend far beyond immediate resource tracking. A naturalist therefore needs an account of why mechanisms calibrated for practical ecological problems transfer reliably into abstract theoretical domains. The point does not assume such transfer fails; it identifies a further bridge required before local adaptive accuracy can justify global confidence in reflective cognition.

novelty.explanation: This is a new domain-transfer line that distinguishes ecological reliability from abstract worldview reasoning without attributing it to Plantinga.

newArguments.title: A calibrated undercutting threshold
newArguments.text: The defeater can be formulated without claiming that every faculty-produced belief collapses simultaneously. If the believer's own theory makes systematic reliability uncertain in the domains used to endorse that theory, confidence should be reduced in proportion to the breadth and relevance of the uncertainty. This localized, graded undercutting model avoids universal skepticism while preserving self-reference: the critical question becomes whether independent calibration can restore confidence precisely where naturalism and evolution are assessed.

novelty.explanation: This replaces universal defeat transmission with a graded, domain-sensitive model responsive to the transcript's overstatement.

thesis.text: The strongest reply is that naturalism and evolution can support fallible but generally reliable cognition through converging environmental, causal, social, and corrective mechanisms, so the EAAN's required low-or-inscrutable reliability premise is not established.

novelty.explanation: This combines Law's live mechanisms into a single proportionate reliability thesis while expressly retaining fallibility.

premises.text: Accurate representations of stable environmental features often enable successful prediction and flexible action across changing circumstances more economically than disconnected false-content systems requiring repeated compensating coincidences.

novelty.explanation: This strengthens the resource-seeking example by emphasizing flexible generalization rather than one isolated successful behavior.

premises.text: Causal interaction with environmental objects, behavioral dispositions, inferential relations, and communicative practices jointly constrain content attribution, making unrestricted substitution of false contents an inadequate model of evolved cognition.

novelty.explanation: This specifies several mutually supporting constraints that were only compressed or implicit in Law's live account.

premises.text: General cognitive reliability does not require every belief to be true; it requires truth-conducive performance under relevant conditions, with predictable limitations, correctable biases, and domain-sensitive calibration.

novelty.explanation: This directly repairs the missing answer to Plantinga's aggregate model by replacing conjunction with calibrated tendency.

premises.text: Learning, interpersonal criticism, measurement, and cultural accumulation can amplify and correct biologically evolved capacities, so present reliability need not equal the unaided accuracy of an ancestral individual organism.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a new cumulative-correction mechanism absent from the locked transcript moves.

premises.text: Because naturalism can offer positive though defeasible reliability mechanisms, recognizing evolution does not by itself generate the higher-order doubt required to defeat trust in the faculties used to assess naturalism and evolution.

novelty.explanation: This connects the positive evolutionary account directly to the defeater stage that Law's closing summary only partially addressed.

conclusion.text: Therefore, unless the pro case defeats these converging truth-conducive and error-corrective mechanisms, naturalism plus evolution does not warrant the general reliability doubt needed to produce the proposed self-referential defeater.

novelty.explanation: This supplies the missing explicit bridge from Law's reliability defense to rejection of the motion-level defeater.

newArguments.title: Convergent calibration without circularity
newArguments.text: Reliability assessment need not rest on one undifferentiated faculty certifying itself. Perception, memory, prediction, testimony, instrumentation, and controlled intervention can generate partially independent checks whose disagreements expose error and whose convergence supports calibrated confidence. Although every check uses some cognitive capacity, their different causal pathways reduce dependence on a single failure mode. Naturalism can therefore answer the self-reference concern with networked calibration rather than an impossible viewpoint wholly outside cognition.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a new network-calibration response to self-reference rather than merely repeating evolutionary resource tracking.

newArguments.title: Asymmetric costs of systematic error
newArguments.text: Plantinga's even-odds model treats true and false contents as if adaptive outcomes were broadly indifferent between them. Across variable environments, however, systematically false representations often require fragile compensating desires or behavioral mappings, while approximately accurate representations support successful action across many contexts. Selection need not inspect propositions semantically; differential robustness can favor architectures whose contents track recurring environmental structures. This supplies a probabilistic reason against equal truth odds without claiming universal accuracy.

novelty.explanation: This repairs Law's missing response to the equal-odds aggregation by providing a robustness-based asymmetry.
